scope: Ovarian carcinoma, WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours 5th ed. (2020). Histotype is the classification spine; the five major epithelial histotypes are distinct diseases. Internal substrate only.

classification_records.morphology: Papillary/solid/glandular growth with marked nuclear atypia, high mitotic rate; often tubal (STIC) origin.
ihc_signature: p53 aberrant (mutant pattern: null or overexpression)
molecular_signature: BRCA1/2 and homologous-recombination deficiency in a large subset
classification_records.grading_system: Binary high-grade (HGSC is by definition high-grade; low-grade serous is a separate entity)
classification_records.clinical_note: The most common and lethal ovarian carcinoma. WT1 + aberrant-p53 IHC defines it; HRD/BRCA status drives PARP-inhibitor therapy.

classification_records.morphology: Uniform low-grade nuclei, micropapillary/papillary architecture, low mitotic rate; arises from serous borderline tumor.
classification_records.grading_system: Low-grade (distinct entity from HGSC, not a grade of it)
classification_records.clinical_note: Biologically distinct from HGSC: wild-type p53, MAPK-driven, more indolent but chemo-resistant; MEK-inhibitor relevance.

classification_records.morphology: Clear/hobnail cells, papillary/tubulocystic/solid patterns; endometriosis association.
classification_records.grading_system: Considered high-grade by default; conventional grading not applied
classification_records.clinical_note: Endometriosis-associated; relatively chemo-resistant. Napsin A/HNF1-beta positive, WT1 negative — a clean IHC separation from serous.

classification_records.morphology: Glandular architecture resembling endometrial endometrioid carcinoma; squamous morules; endometriosis association.
molecular_signature: ARID1A, PTEN, CTNNB1, PIK3CA; mismatch-repair deficiency in a subset
classification_records.clinical_note: WT1-negative, ER/PR-positive; MMR testing relevant (Lynch association). Distinguish from serous by WT1/p53.

classification_records.morphology: Gastrointestinal-type mucinous epithelium; expansile vs infiltrative invasion; must exclude metastasis.
classification_records.clinical_note: Primary ovarian mucinous carcinoma is rare; the critical task is excluding a GI/appendiceal or pancreaticobiliary metastasis (SATB2/CK20/CDX2 panel). HER2 testing relevant.

notes: Histotype IS the classification (five distinct diseases, not grades of one). The WT1 + p53 IHC pair is the master discriminator: HGSC (WT1+/p53 aberrant) vs LGSC (WT1+/p53 wild-type) vs clear cell & endometrioid (WT1-). Verify IHC patterns at write time.
